macro.narrative: Re-anchored Fri 21 Aug 10:10 SGT on complete Wed 19 AND Thu 20 Aug sessions (a two-session catch-up from the prior Tue-18-Aug anchor). Wednesday's dominant catalyst was the US Treasury's surprise announcement to double its long-bond buyback operation size (to >=$4bn/operation for 10-30y, effective 9 Sep-4 Nov) after the 30-year yield hit its highest level since 2007 (~5.33%). This pulled the 10y down 6bp to 4.647% and the 30y down 9bp to 5.196%, sent the dollar to an 11-week low, and ignited a REAL real-yield-driven rally in gold (GLD +3.84%) and silver (SLV +4.47%) that flowed through with operating leverage into miners (GDX +9.42%, SILJ +9.55%, Barrick +8.82%) — unlike the Monday-17-Aug futures-roll false breakout corrected two runs ago. That relief came too late to stop a continuing Asia chip-sector rout that began Tue 18 Aug (Nvidia lost as much as ~$600bn intraday on AI 'circular financing' fears): Nikkei -3.16% and KOSPI -5.80% Wednesday as Samsung and SK Hynix were hammered. July FOMC minutes (released Wed) showed an unusually visible 3-of-12 dissent favoring a hike — hawkish, but markets largely looked through it given the buyback-driven yield relief. Thursday reversed the cross-currents again: blockbuster US data (jobless claims 206K vs 210K forecast; Philly Fed manufacturing 47.4 vs 24.1 forecast, a huge beat) trimmed near-term Fed-cut odds, and St. Louis Fed's Musalem said he 'won't prejudge' September while flagging inflation still running 2.5-3% against the 2% target — a hawkish cocktail that, layered on lingering AI-valuation anxiety, drove a genuine equity selloff (S&P -0.87% to 7,641.16, Nasdaq -1.00%, Dow -1.32%, Russell -1.34%, VIX +7.52% to 16.01) while gold/silver kept grinding higher (GLD +0.34%, SLV +2.75%) on the still-easier real-yield/dollar backdrop, even as miners' momentum decelerated (GDX +2.59%, SILJ +0.67%) as equity-market risk-off capped their equity beta. Asia bifurcated sharply Thursday: KOSPI +5.89% (Samsung's >KRW100tn shareholder-return plan and SK Hynix's ~KRW40tn buyback/cancellation, plus the buyback-driven yield relief) nearly fully reversed Wednesday's crash, Nikkei +1.36% partially recovered on chip dip-buying, and Hang Seng's more modest +0.80% reflected calmer, idiosyncratic HK flows (Tencent/Xiaomi up, SMIC down). Separately, Brent/WTI continued grinding higher (+2.29%/+1.05% Thu) on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz crisis (ADNOC tankers attacked Thu evening; Trump announced sweeping new Iran sanctions Tue) — a structural driver largely independent of the gold/equity story. Bitcoin surged on the same debasement narrative plus a record ~$2.7-3bn short-liquidation cascade, reaching a ~$74,859 Friday-morning level (a continuous-trading LEVEL, not a session close). Risk-on cut from 0.45 to 0.38: a genuine US equity selloff with a real VIX spike, hawkish Fed cross-currents (a rare 3-way FOMC dissent plus a hawkish regional president), and unresolved AI-valuation anxiety are risk-negative, only partially offset by the Treasury-buyback yield relief and idiosyncratic (not broad-based) Asia strength.
